overview: After 2.f4 exf4 White develops the queen at once with 3.Qf3, hitting f4 and f7 and eyeing the Bc4 follow-up, instead of the standard 3.Nf3 or 3.Bc4. Black keeps the pawn with ...Nc6 and ...Nf6 or hits the queen with ...d5. White gets a lead in development and pressure on f7, but the queen is exposed and the position is considered inferior to the main King's Gambit lines.

white_ideas.idea: Recover f4 or play Bc4 and Nc3 with pressure on f7
Use the open f-file after castling

black_ideas.idea: Keep the extra pawn with ...Nc6, ...Nf6 and ...d5
Hit the queen with tempo and develop with ...Qh4+ ideas

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with the f4 pawn gone and White queen on f3

character.notes: An early queen and a pawn sacrifice give mutual attacking chances and quick tactics.

gambit.notes: White offers the f-pawn for development; Black can hold it with ...Nc6 or ...Nf6.

soundness.notes: The early queen move leaves White slightly worse against accurate play, and strong players avoid it.

structure.notes: The f-file and centre open, with e4 attacked early.

approach.notes: A rare side line of the King's Gambit, not used by elite players.

level.notes: Needs some knowledge of the tactics, but no long forced theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Black returns the pawn
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. f4 exf4 3. Qf3 d5 4. exd5
sublines_that_differ.how: Black hits the centre at once and the queen move can look a tempo lost.

character.reason: A gambit with an early queen leads to mutual attacks and tactics.

gambit.reason: White gives the f-pawn and Black can keep it with ...Nc6 and ...Nf6.

soundness.reason: The queen move wastes time compared with the main King's Gambit lines.

structure.reason: Central and f-file lines open up from the start.

level.reason: It needs judgement about the exposed queen; a Dubious line is never Beginner.

plans.reason: White's idea is a lead in development and f7 pressure with the queen out early.
